Getting through / ongoing

NEW granular check: 0% HTTP/3 vs 12% on the rest of the key, Windows fonts on a non-Windows UA 92% vs 5%, one exact font set 78% vs 29%, one voices hash 72% vs 46%. NEW check - fingerprint detail (cohort profile, 7th indicator)

  • Added from the Blizzard ROW 'candidate signals vs truth' work: per cohort vs the rest of the key - HTTP/3 share (FP bound: real Chrome upgrades to QUIC, libraries don't), HTTP/1.1 share, fonts that don't match the claimed OS, <=4GB memory with 12+ cores (rig), one exact font set / one voices hash reused, no fonts / no fingerprint. Counts when 2+ fire. Cohort scores are now out of 7 (3+ = attack-like).

Traffic drops — check with the customer, not attacks

Every Production key whose traffic fell below 40% of its own normal: a whole window day vs its median baseline day (≥5k/day), the last 6 complete hours or the last complete hour vs the same hours on the 7 previous days. A drop on one key while the same customer's other keys are normal usually means the page stopped calling Arkose (outage, maintenance, integration or key-config change). On drop days the share-of-traffic check is skipped for that key.

Share of key traffic — false-positive check (window 2026-11-21 → 2026-11-24 vs 7-day baseline)

Rule: a signal should flag under 2% of a key's total traffic. Above that it is marked FP risk, unless the key's traffic itself jumped ≥1.5× its baseline that day and the flagged sessions explain ≥50% of the jump (volumetric attack: the attack is the extra traffic, so a high share is expected). A signal that already flags >2% of the key's baseline traffic is FP risk regardless. Per day, key/day pairs with ≥1k flagged.

Share of key traffic — false-positive check (window 2026-11-21 → 2026-11-24 vs 7-day baseline)

Rule: a signal should flag under 2% of a key's total traffic. Above that it is marked FP risk, unless the key's traffic itself jumped ≥1.5× its baseline that day and the flagged sessions explain ≥50% of the jump (volumetric attack: the attack is the extra traffic, so a high share is expected). A signal that already flags >2% of the key's baseline traffic is FP risk regardless. Per day, key/day pairs with ≥1k flagged.

Above that it is marked FP risk, unless the key's traffic itself jumped ≥1.5× its baseline that day and the flagged sessions explain ≥50% of the jump (volumetric attack: the attack is the extra traffic, so a high share is expected).
